title: Speaker-Independent Speech Synthesis from Real-time MRI Articulatory Data
abstract: This paper proposes a speaker-independent speech synthesis method that generates speech waveforms from real-time MRI (rtMRI) videos. The proposed model uses EfficientNetV2 for per-frame feature extraction, E-Branchformer for temporal modeling, and BigVGAN-v2 for speech synthesis. Speaker characteristics are acquired from rtMRI videos through cross-modal training with speaker embeddings, enabling speaker-independent synthesis from rtMRI videos alone. Experiments using the USC 75-Speaker Speech MRI Database demonstrate that the proposed method achieves favorable linguistic accuracy for read speech in a speaker-independent setting. F0 correlation analysis indicates that relative prosodic patterns are captured to a reasonable extent, as expected from visual articulatory information, though absolute F0 estimation remains challenging. Speaker similarity results show that although within-gender speaker discrimination proved difficult, speaker identity is reproduced to a reasonable degree.
relevance_note: Speaker-independent speech synthesis from real-time MRI articulatory video; biosignal-to-speech, consistent with rejected silent-speech precedents (2510.23969 emg2speech, 2607.18629 CS-ETS).
